---
title: "Typst format"
subtitle: "Document types, page decoration, and section pages."
description: "Worked examples of the mcanouil-typst options, and of the mapping that sends a div class to a Typst function."
---

`mcanouil-typst` produces a PDF through Typst.
The [rendered report](../preview.pdf) on this site is built by it as the site publishes.

The [Reference](../reference.qmd#mcanouil-typst) lists every option and its default.
This page shows what each one changes.

## The report on this site

```yaml
---
title: "The Typst format"
subtitle: "Rendered by the documentation site"
author: "Mickaël CANOUIL"
date: last-modified
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    style: professional
    brand-mode: light
---
```

## Document type

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    document-type: letter
```

`document-type` takes `report`, `invoice`, `letter`, or `cv`, and it is matched without regard to case.
It chooses the template the document is built from, so it changes the structure of the page rather than its colours.
The default is `report`.

## Page decoration

Five options control the decoration, and each defaults to on.

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    show-corner-brackets: false
    show-margin-decoration: false
    show-title-page-background: false
    show-heading-underlines: false
    show-logo: false
```

- `show-corner-brackets` draws the signature brackets at the page corners.
- `show-margin-decoration` draws coloured bars along the margins.
- `show-title-page-background` draws the geometric background on the title page.
- `show-heading-underlines` draws the gradient underline below a heading.
- `show-logo` puts the logo in the header.

Turning all five off gives a plain document that keeps the typography and the palette.
That is the setting to use when a document must be printed in one colour.

## Section pages

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    section-page: true
    section-pagebreak: true
```

`section-page` puts a title page before each top-level section.
`section-pagebreak` puts a page break before that title page.

Both default to on, which suits a long report.
A short document reads better with both off, because a two-page note does not need a title page for each of its sections.

## Lists of figures and tables

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    list-of: false
```

`list-of` includes the list of figures and the list of tables after the table of contents.
It defaults to on.

## Brand mode

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    brand-mode: dark
```

`brand-mode` chooses between the light and the dark palette, and defaults to `light` here.
A Reveal.js deck defaults to `dark` instead, so a document and a deck built from the same brand do not match unless one of them says so.

## Sending a class to a Typst function

The extension maps a div or a span class to a Typst function.
The built-in mappings cover the components, and a document can add its own:

```yaml
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    typst-markdown:
      divs:
        note: my-note
      spans:
        sidenote:
          function: my-sidenote
          arguments: true
```

The four keys are `divs`, `spans`, `tables`, and `images`.

A plain function name wraps the content and passes no attributes.
A table needs a `function:` key, and `arguments: true` passes the element's attributes to the function as named arguments.
A table with no `function:` key is reported as a warning and ignored, and the render carries on.

The class is then written as an ordinary fenced div:

```markdown
::: {.note}

The content this function receives.

:::
```

The function has to exist in the template scope, so this is for a document that already supplies its own Typst partials.
